text:
alex: Hey team — hitting a weird flow onboarding a new coworker. They followed the Docker quickstart, built the container, and when they run the example it returns a 403. Error body says: "403 Forbidden: workspace activation required (billing)" but the billing page shows the org has a card on file.

sam: ugh. two quick checks: 1) is the API key actually available inside the container (env var exported)? 2) are there any HTTP proxies / SSL interceptors messing with TLS?

alex: they set REDWOOD_API_KEY in the Dockerfile via ARG then ENV. when they run `docker run -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=$REDWOOD_API_KEY my-quickstart` it prints the key in env and the app sends it. curl from the host to `https://api.redwood.example/v1/models` using the same key works. inside the container `curl -v` shows a TLS handshake but response is the 403 body above.

maya: can you paste the exact curl command and the 403 JSON? also paste `env | grep -i proxy` from inside the container. sometimes corporate proxy injects a captive cert and the service returns a different error.

alex: sure: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}' -H "Content-Type: application/json" -w "\nHTTP_CODE:%{http_code}\n"`
Response:
```
{"error":"workspace activation required","code":"billing_required","message":"Please enable billing for your workspace to make this request."}
HTTP_CODE:403
```
Inside container `env | grep -i proxy` => `http_proxy=http://proxy.corp:3128` and `https_proxy=http://proxy.corp:3128`.

liam: aha. corporate proxies often rewrite TLS or require interception which can break cert pinning / SNI. But the 403 JSON with billing_required is odd — that usually comes from our backend when the workspace id we sent is recognized but not active. Are you using an API key that is scoped to the host (e.g., workspace-bound) and maybe host header got mangled by the proxy?

sam: also check NO_PROXY. If you have the proxy env set, the request may be routed through a proxy that rewrites host headers. Try setting `NO_PROXY=api.redwood.ai,api.redwood.local` or unset `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` for that container and retry.

alex: good call. I unset the proxy env and ran the same curl inside the container — success! got 200 and a token stream. So the proxy was the culprit.

maya: cool. two follow-ups to prevent future onboarding friction: 1) we should add a troubleshooting bullet in the quickstart about proxy envs and setting NO_PROXY for api.redwood.ai, especially for Docker. 2) add a short FAQ entry for the exact 403 JSON pointing to common causes (billing vs proxy vs wrong key).

devx-bot: Created ticket #DX-487: "Quickstart: Docker proxy env causes 403/billing_required". Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/DX-487 :link:

sam: also we should add a CLI diagnoser in the quickstart that runs a small `curl -I https://api.redwood.ai -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY"` and prints helpful hints when it sees a 403 with code billing_required (e.g., "Check workspace billing -> link", "Check proxy envs -> run: env | grep -i proxy").

alex: agreed. I'll add a PR for the quickstart readme + a tiny shell check and link the PR in the ticket. Thanks all :pray:
